title: Say why a plan failed and why a project waits

expected.says: Run's report for the demo export matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def deletion_filter(built: Built, keep: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> list[str]
blueprint.contract: Returns, sorted, the names of an irreducible set of rows that cannot all hold: relax each row in name order, keep it relaxed while the model stays infeasible, restore it when relaxing it makes the model feasible. Rows named in keep are never relaxed.
blueprint.idea: The deletion filter: the rows you cannot relax without the clash disappearing form a conflict, and dropping any one of them gives a plan.

blueprint.contract: True unless HiGHS reports the model infeasible: only the termination INFEASIBLE counts as no plan, and INFEASIBLE_OR_UNBOUNDED counts as feasible (every variable is binary, so the model is never unbounded).
blueprint.idea: The filter only asks one question of each solve: does a plan exist?

lesson.title: 9.1.1 Infeasible, Unbounded, or the Solver Can't Tell

blueprint.signature: def describe(request: Request, name: str) -> str
blueprint.contract: Returns one row in the planners' words, read from its name: `spend in <y> within $<b>k`, `<id> is a must-do`, `<id> is forced in`, `at most one of <ids>` (the group's members in id order, joined by a comma and a space), `<a> and <b> are funded together or not at all`, `<child> started by <t> needs <parent> started by <t - lag>`, `remove at least $<floor>k of risk` (one decimal, thousands commas) for the risk floor; the name itself for any other row. The kind is the part of the name before its first underscore.
blueprint.idea: A conflict is only useful in the names people can change.

lesson.title: 9.1.6 Turning an IIS Into a Planner Message

blueprint.signature: def explain(request: Request, rows: list[str]) -> Conflict
blueprint.contract: Returns a Conflict with the rows and a message: `No plan meets these <n> rules together; drop or change any one of them:` then one line `  <row>: <description>` per row.
blueprint.idea: Turn the IIS into a message that says what to change.

blueprint.contract: None when the request has a plan; otherwise the Conflict of the rows that clash.

lesson.title: 9.1.3 IIS With MathOpt, gurobipy and Pyomo

blueprint.signature: def why_deferred(request: Request, plan, project_id: str) -> Deferral
blueprint.contract: Forces the project in with a row `force_<id>`. When that is feasible, returns the NPV the plan gives up and the funded projects it drops; when it is not, the Conflict of the rows that block it, the force row kept.
blueprint.idea: Forcing a decision in and re-solving prices it; when no plan exists, the conflict says why.

lesson.title: 9.3.2 Why Selected, Why Deferred: Forcing In and Out

blueprint.signature: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int
blueprint.contract: Prints the report; for an infeasible request also prints the conflict message and returns 1. With --why PROJECT for a project the plan leaves out, prints `<id> cannot be funded. <message>` or `Funding <id> costs $<cost>k of NPV and drops <ids or nothing>.` (cost in whole $k, ids joined by a comma and a space); for a project the plan funds, nothing more.
blueprint.idea: The command line is where the planners read the diagnostics.

lesson.title: 14.2.6 Why It Failed, Why It Was Deferred: A Diagnostics Layer

cases: an infeasible request names exactly the rules that clash
a budget row that plays no part in the clash is left out of the conflict
the message states each clashing rule in the planners' words
a deferred project's cost is the NPV given up and the projects dropped
a project that cannot be funded is explained by the rows that block it
the command line explains an infeasible request
a conflict names an alternative group by its members and states the risk floor in $k
asking why about a project the plan funds prints the report and nothing more
